currentManifestItem.title: A conical helicity packet has reduced axial spin projection

references.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology

currentManifestItem.statement:
Let $	heta(\mathbf k)=\arccos(k_z/|\mathbf k|)\in[0,\pi]$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$, $	heta_0\in[0,\pi]$, and $0<\delta\le\pi$, a normalized helicity-$\sigma$ packet of angular width $\delta$ is a vector $f\in\mathcal H_T^
u$ with $\|f\|_
u=1$, $P_\sigma f=f$ almost everywhere, and $f(\mathbf k)=0$ almost everywhere unless $|	heta(\mathbf k)-	heta_0|\le\delta$. Such packets exist for every $	heta_0$ and $\delta$. Each satisfies $$\left|\langle f,S_z'fangle_
u-\hbar\sigma\cos	heta_0ight|\le\hbar\delta.$$ Consequently, for any sequence $0<\delta_m\le\pi$ with $\delta_m\downarrow0$ and normalized helicity-$\sigma$ packets $f_m$ of widths $\delta_m$, $\langle f_m,S_z'f_mangle_
u	o\hbar\sigma\cos	heta_0$. An ideal delta-supported Bessel mode, defined here as a generalized amplitude supported on the exact cone $\{\mathbf k\in M:	heta(\mathbf k)=	heta_0\}$ (or a smaller fixed-radius conical shell), is not a nonzero vector of $\mathcal H_T^
u$ and cannot be normalized.
